response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT ID, HGB*1.0/HCT AS r FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0), p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(r) AS ratio FROM t GROUP BY ID), o AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS a FROM p), k AS (SELECT p.ID, p.ratio, p.ratio - o.a AS d1 FROM p, o WHERE p.ratio > o.a), s AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS a2 FROM k), f AS (SELECT k.ratio, k.d1, k.ratio - s.a2 AS d2 FROM k, s WHERE k.ratio > s.a2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_second FROM f

assumptions.assumption: Ratios that can't be computed are tests where HGB or HCT is NULL or HCT is 0; these are excluded.
The 'average ratio across all patients' is the mean of the per-patient average ratios (each patient weighted equally), not a mean over all individual tests.
Patients with no computable ratio are excluded from every average. The second average is the mean of the kept group's per-patient ratios.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is pooled over every individual test ratio, so patients with more tests weigh more. The rest of the logic is unchanged.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT ID, HGB*1.0/HCT AS r FROM Laboratory WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0), p AS (SELECT ID, AVG(r) AS ratio FROM t GROUP BY ID), o AS (SELECT AVG(r) AS a FROM t), k AS (SELECT p.ID, p.ratio, p.ratio - o.a AS d1 FROM p, o WHERE p.ratio > o.a), s AS (SELECT AVG(ratio) AS a2 FROM k), f AS (SELECT k.ratio, k.d1, k.ratio - s.a2 AS d2 FROM k, s WHERE k.ratio > s.a2) SELECT AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(d1) AS avg_above_overall, AVG(d2) AS avg_above_second FROM f
